analysis: The change is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md adds two table rows (head lines 316-317) for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. Both are kill-switch-style env vars (0/false/no/off disable; default on) that govern Qwen inline-MTP scheduling, with readers in libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../MTPContractsV2.swift. The rows state they are not forwarded to LaunchAgents. They have no effect on the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-011), key custody (A-002/A-003), or the prefix-cache at-rest posture (T-041). The patch adds no code and changes no security configuration. The only mildly relevant point is that the carry and chained settings alter speculative decode scheduling and hidden-state handling, i.e. performance and scheduling behavior rather than trust or encryption. The corresponding code change (not in the supplied batch) would need its own review for the interaction with the prefix cache, KV state and per-request isolation (T-028, T-041). The documented claim of non-forwarding to launchd cannot be verified against LaunchAgent.swift from the supplied evidence. This is a documentation accuracy question, not a security regression. The patch excerpt is marked incomplete, but the head range map is complete at 316-317 and shows only these two insertions. No findings.
